title: Your first things keep their day
highlights: When you start, a first thing written for tomorrow stays tomorrow, as its chip said; today's lines become your Top 3

title: Saves that leave sooner
highlights: Changes on the calendar reach your other devices about three times sooner: dropping a task into a Time Slot saves in under half a second instead of more than one

title: Tell any AI to do anything
highlights: Your AI assistant can now do what you can in the app: 51 actions over MCP, from tasks, Inbox, projects and labels to calendar, Time Slots, routines, focus, Plan my day, Shut down, the library and settings
Your journal and the people you keep stay out of its reach unless you switch them on for that key, in Settings → AI assistants
Deleting or moving a Time block keeps its tasks right, and rescheduling a task takes it out of its slot
Each release now also builds the Microsoft Store package for Windows

title: Links that open, and the apps one tap away
highlights: In the Windows and Android apps, links open in your browser, so Connect Google Calendar works from there too
Get the apps from a bar in your browser or Settings → App; the links always fetch the newest version
New versions are announced within a few hours of release, no longer once a day

title: Your plan in Google, reminders for events, and Undo for everything
highlights: Your time blocks, scheduled tasks and events can show in your main Google calendar as private busy time. Reconnect Google once in Settings to allow it
Remind me before an event: at start, 5, 10, 15, 30 minutes or an hour before, for one event or the whole series
Time Slots on the phone, “Into a slot…” in every task’s menu, and >Code block in the bar
Undo for every change that used to happen silently, and keys for priority, focus, goal, someday, duration and Plan
⌘/Ctrl+↑/↓ moves a task up or down in any list
Old journal entries, quotes and notes come back to you, like old tasks do
Chat keeps your conversation until you clear it, and you can talk to it
Save a project’s checklist as a template and use it on another project

title: Repairs, and updates that install in place
highlights: Activity your AI assistant logged while its bug was live is repaired, so it counts like everything else
The Android app is now signed with its permanent key: after one last reinstall, updates install over the top
The privacy policy has a real address to write to

title: Time Slots and your Google calendars
highlights: Time Slots: drop tasks into a Time block like “Code block” and it holds them, with a checklist and how full it is; move the slot and its tasks move too
Repeating slots hold tasks for each day, and a task comes out of its slot with Undo
Google Calendar, read-only: connect in Settings, pick calendars like your prayer times, and they show on your calendar as busy. Kai’s Flow never changes them and never sends them to the AI
The privacy policy now also lives on the app’s own address

title: A privacy page on the app, ready for Google Calendar
highlights: The privacy policy now lives on the app's own address too, and says exactly what Google Calendar sync will do: read the calendars you choose, never change them

title: Your assistant plans the week, and keys for everything
highlights: Your AI assistant can plan your week: reschedule and edit tasks, add, move or delete events and Time blocks. Adding a task over MCP works again
Ctrl+Z undoes the last thing you did; i, u and / jump to Inbox, Upcoming and Search; ⌘K reaches projects, areas and labels
The calendar has keys: d, w, m, 1–7, ← → and t, and ⌘-click on a slot makes a task
The bar understands more: “every week”, // for notes, <friday, links, and events. The tray follows the same rules
A timed capture filed from the Inbox lands on the calendar; “Ends after N times” really ends, and Yearly is a repeat
After midnight, Shut down closes the day you lived, and the evening nudge stays quiet once you have
Birthdays a week ahead, archived projects stop slipping, and routines get a description
On a phone, the journal's controls are easier to tap and a tap on your words never deletes the entry; a paused series stays quiet everywhere

title: Journal photos that go when you say so
highlights: Photos leave with their journal entry: once an entry is deleted for good, its photos are removed from storage too
A day with only a photo counts as written, for Day N, the week's kept days and your Kept count
On a phone, a photo's × is easier to hit without catching the photo beside it

title: A redesigned day, events that repeat, and your notebook
highlights: Today follows your reviewed design: one date, a Now card while something runs, and today's three
Events open the menu you drew and repeat as a real series; planning mode folds the calendar while you place tasks
The Notebook page: your plan as a page to copy into your journal, print, and bring back by photo
A calmer Inbox, a Search that finds your Library, and labels you can pick, rename and colour
Edit everything after you make it, routines included, with minutes per step and a plant of their own
Undo instead of “are you sure” everywhere, and the night look: frosted cards, the moonflower, two fireflies
Routine reminders really send, the hourly Overdue push is gone, and a pick moved to another day leaves your Top 3 (older ones were cleared once)
Typed captures are filled in by the AI (Groq), and the privacy page now says so

title: AI assistants load their tools
highlights: Claude Code and other new AI assistants now load Kai's Flow's tools: the tool list carries the cache hints the newest protocol requires

title: Notifications that arrive, and a calmer look
highlights: Notifications reach the Windows app and the Android phone: reminders, the morning digest and the evening nudge
A Send a test notification button shows exactly what is in the way on this device
Settings redesigned: one tidy row for every setting, two columns on wide screens
Easier to read everywhere: stronger faint text and no more tiny labels

title: The garden on your home screen
highlights: 34 home-screen widgets for Android: Today, Top 3 and the goal, capture, calendar, focus, routines, Inbox, Overdue, rituals and more
Tick tasks and routines, stop or finish focus, and capture without opening the app
Every widget follows your phone's dark mode, and a setting hides task names on the home screen

title: From a while ago, settled
highlights: From a while ago says what it is and how old, and opens when you tap it
Every button settles it: Plan, Done, Let it go, or Not now with the real wait shown
Put something off twice and it asks once: keep it or let it go

title: AI assistants can connect
highlights: The MCP server for AI assistants starts again: it crashed on start-up, so connecting with your AI access key always failed

title: Plan, replan, and a calmer day
highlights: Plan or Replan any task: Next free slot (you confirm it), Tomorrow first thing, and your own weekend days
Make any task the goal of the day and put your Top 3 in your order, the same on your phone and computer
The calendar's side rail shows Overdue, Today and Inbox, and a time (even one typed in a capture) puts a task on the calendar
Move tasks into a domain, an area or a project, Ctrl+A works on every list, and the sync line stays quiet
New sounds (Felt by default, or Kalimba and Glass), and a short tour with a searchable Guide
Phone polish: a + capture button, tidier Routines, readable short calendar blocks

title: Capture that types, and fills itself in
highlights: Tap Capture to type: on your phone the keyboard comes up with the sheet, and desktop has a Capture button
Hold to talk, or tap the mic in the sheet; on desktop the mic dictates into the field so you can check it first
Write it the way you'd say it: the AI picks up the date, time, priority, length and notes, no !!! or // needed
Whatever the AI filled in shows in a note with Undo, and anything you typed yourself always wins
A What's new page, and a heads-up in Settings → App when an update is ready

title: Your own time zone, and easier projects
highlights: Your own time zone: Today, reminders and the morning digest follow your clock, wherever you are
AI assistants can read and add to your days over MCP, with a key you make in Settings
Rename a project or area from inside it, and change what a thing is: project, retainer, area or domain
Domains can be made, renamed, recoloured, merged and deleted from anywhere
Search results open the thing itself, and a project’s status updates can be edited
Easier number fields: tap to select, or nudge with − and +

title: A tray icon, and paper that becomes tasks
highlights: A tray icon on Windows, with a little flyout: now, next, your Top 3, quick capture and focus
Notifications with buttons — Done and Tomorrow right from a reminder
Quiet hours, and task names hidden on the lock screen until you choose
Paper capture: photograph your handwritten notes and they come back as tasks, events and notes (Arabic too)
Signing up works straight away while email is being set up
Sign-up and reset emails lead back to the app
The chat answers from your day and knows how the app works — in your language
GitHub in Settings leads straight to your issues

title: Settings that tell the truth, and the share sheet
highlights: Settings tells the truth: real reminder times, the real GitHub state, and Google Calendar marked as coming
Kai’s Flow is in the Android share sheet
Make capture keys on the phone
Labels on task rows, and *label to add one
Streak goals for routines
Retainer projects roll their open tasks into the new month

title: Settings that scroll, and a calendar that snaps
highlights: Settings scrolls everywhere
Our own right-click menu
Delete areas
Search in Focus
The calendar snaps to 15 minutes
A default calendar view
Check for updates
A Windows installer that looks like the app
Plan my day searches all your tasks and lets you pick in place
A calendar task opens in one tap
Reminders move with their task
Routines fold by time of day
The pressing ceremony waits for you
Import from Todoist, TickTick, Notion, Obsidian, Kindle and Goodreads
The new icon: a Source Serif K on warm paper
A touch calendar for phones: swipe days, hold to move, resize handles
Open a task as a sheet over any page
A calmer first run
Plan my day and Shut down, redrawn
Our own date and time pickers
Today on the phone, with the NOW slip
Swipe right for Tomorrow, left for Trash with Undo
Hold to select
The refreshed design system
The native Android app
The phone pass: readability, phone type, tab icons
GitHub issues into your Inbox
Capture from anywhere with a link
